-- True when the path never climbs above its starting directory
-- and is not absolute. Names such as "sub/../a.txt" stay inside.
stays_inside(path: str) -> bool =
  ex stays_inside("a.txt") == True
  ex stays_inside("sub/../a.txt") == True
  ex stays_inside("sub/x.txt") == True
  ex stays_inside("..") == False
  ex stays_inside("/etc/passwd") == False
  ex stays_inside("sub/../../x") == False
  if path.split("\\").len() > 1
    return False
  let parts = path.split("/")
  let first = parts.get(0) else ""
  if first == ""
    return False
  var depth = 0
  for part in parts
    if part == ".."
      depth -= 1
      if depth < 0
        return False
    else if part == "" or part == "."
      continue
    else
      depth += 1
  True

-- Reads the file at `path` inside `notes`, or "" when the path leaves
-- `notes` or the file is missing or unreadable.
read_public(path: str) -> str uses fs =
  ex read_public("..") == ""
  ex read_public("/etc/passwd") == ""
  ex read_public("sub/../../x") == ""
  ex read_public("missing.txt") == ""
  var result = ""
  if stays_inside(path)
    with fs = fs.sub("notes")
      result = fs.read(path) else ""
  result

test_stays_inside() =
  assert stays_inside("sub/../a.txt")
  assert not stays_inside("../a.txt")
  assert not stays_inside("/a.txt")

test_read_public_escape() uses fs =
  assert read_public("../x") == ""
  assert read_public("sub/../../x") == ""
